ap_calculus_ab-f01.title: Accumulation function of a current: value, Fundamental Theorem derivative, average rate, absolute maximum, concavity

stimulus.description: Current into a battery and the net charge delivered

data.model: I(t) = 4e^(-t/4) sin(0.8t) amperes, 0 <= t <= 8 seconds; Q(x) = integral of I(t) from 0 to x

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: During a charging test, the current into a small battery is modeled by $I(t)=4e^{-t/4}\sin(0.8t)$ amperes (coulombs per second), where $t$ is the time in seconds and $0\le t\le 8$. The net charge delivered to the battery during the first $x$ seconds is $Q(x)=\int_0^x I(t)\,dt$ coulombs. Find $Q(3)$ and $Q'(3)$.
parts.model_answer: $Q(3)=\int_0^{3} I(t)\,dt=5.688$ coulombs. By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, $Q'(3)=I(3)=1.276$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of the accumulated charge, using the definite integral of the current
Uses the Fundamental Theorem: the derivative of Q equals the integrand evaluated at the endpoint

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of $Q$ over the interval $2\le x\le 7$. Using correct units, state what this average rate of change represents.
parts.model_answer: $\dfrac{Q(7)-Q(2)}{7-2}=0.065$ coulombs per second: the average current into the battery between $t=2$ and $t=7$ seconds (it also equals the average value of $I$ on that interval).

rubric_rows.criterion: Average rate of change from the values of Q at the endpoints, divided by the length of the interval
Value with units: coulombs per second (the average current)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: For $0\le x\le 8$, at what value of $x$ does $Q$ attain its absolute maximum value? Find that maximum value and justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $Q'(x)=I(x)=0$ for $x=3.927$ and $x=7.854$. $I$ changes from positive to negative at $x=3.927$, so $Q$ has a local maximum there; $Q(0)=0$, $Q(3.927)=6.262$, $Q(8)=3.920$. The absolute maximum is 6.262 coulombs at $x=3.927$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets the derivative of Q, which is I, equal to zero and finds the critical points in the interval
Justification with the sign of $Q'$, i.e. of $I$: positive then negative at the first critical point
required_elements: $Q'$ changes from positive to negative at $x=3.927$

rubric_rows.criterion: Compares the values of Q at the candidates including both endpoints and states the maximum value

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: On which open intervals within $0<x<8$ is $Q$ concave up? Give a reason for your answer.
parts.model_answer: $Q''(x)=I'(x)$, and $I'(x)>0$ exactly when $Q$ is concave up. $I'(x)=0$ at $x=1.585$, $x=5.512$; the graph of $Q$ is concave up on $0<x<1.585$ and $5.512<x<8$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Reason: relates the concavity of $Q$ to the sign of $Q''=I'$ and finds where $I'$ changes sign
States the intervals on which $I'$ is positive

ap_calculus_ab-f02.title: Cooling model: verify the differential equation, tangent-line estimate, over or under by concavity, time to a target temperature and the rate then

stimulus.description: Temperature of a cast-iron pan cooling in a kitchen

data.model: T(t) = 24 + 196e^(-0.06t) degrees Celsius, t in minutes; dT/dt = -0.06(T - 24)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A cast-iron pan is taken out of an oven and left in a kitchen. Its temperature, in degrees Celsius, is modeled by $T(t)=24+196e^{-0.06t}$, where $t$ is the time in minutes since the pan was taken out. Show that $T$ satisfies the differential equation $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-0.06\,(T-24)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Differentiates the model
Rewrites the exponential term as T minus the room temperature and concludes the equation holds

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve $y=T(t)$ at $t=15$. Use this tangent line to approximate the temperature of the pan at $t=20$.
parts.model_answer: $T(15)=103.688$ and $T'(15)=-4.781$, so the tangent line is $y=103.688+(-4.781)(t-15)$. At $t=20$ the approximation is $79.781$ degrees Celsius.

rubric_rows.criterion: Tangent line equation using the value and the slope at the given time
Approximation at the later time

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Is the approximation in part (b) less than or greater than the actual temperature $T(20)$? Use $\dfrac{d^2T}{dt^2}$ to justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $T''(t)=0.7056e^{-0.06t}>0$, so the graph of $T$ is concave up and lies above its tangent lines. The approximation $79.781$ is less than the actual value $T(20)=83.034$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Justification: the second derivative of the model is positive, so the function is concave up
Conclusion: the tangent line is below a concave up graph, so the approximation is less than the actual temperature

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The pan can be handled safely once its temperature reaches $60$ degrees Celsius. Find the time $t$ at which $T(t)=60$. Using correct units, find the rate of change of the temperature at that time.
parts.model_answer: $T(t)=60$ gives $t=28.243$ minutes. At that time $T'(t)=-0.06(60-24)=-2.160$ degrees Celsius per minute.

rubric_rows.criterion: Equation for the time
Time (calculator)
Rate of change at that time with units: degrees Celsius per minute (negative: the pan is cooling)

ap_calculus_ab-f03.title: Marginal revenue and marginal cost: meaning of marginal profit, best production level, revenue increase, profit at the optimum

stimulus.description: Marginal revenue and marginal cost of a workshop

data.model: MR(q) = 18 - 2ln(q+1), MC(q) = 2 + 0.2q^2, 0 <= q <= 10; q in hundreds of items, money in thousands of dollars; fixed cost 6

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A workshop makes and sells $q$ hundred custom phone cases per week, for $0\le q\le 10$. The marginal revenue is $MR(q)=18-2\ln(q+1)$ and the marginal cost is $MC(q)=2+0.2q^2$, both in thousands of dollars per hundred cases. Find $MR(2)-MC(2)$. Using correct units, explain what this value says about the profit when production is increased from $q=2$.
parts.model_answer: $MR(2)-MC(2)=13.003$ thousand dollars per hundred cases. At $q=2$ the profit is changing at a rate of 13.003 thousand dollars per hundred cases, so producing a little more raises the profit.

rubric_rows.criterion: Difference of the marginal revenue and the marginal cost at the given production level
Interpretation with units: the rate of change of profit, in thousand dollars per hundred cases; positive, so profit increases as production increases
required_elements: rate of change of the profit

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The profit is $P(q)=R(q)-C(q)$, where $R$ and $C$ are the revenue and cost functions. Find the production level $q$ that gives the maximum profit on $0\le q\le 10$. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $P'(q)=MR(q)-MC(q)=0$ at $q=7.644$. $P'>0$ for $q<7.644$ and $P'<0$ for $q>7.644$ on the whole interval, so the maximum profit occurs at $q=7.644$ hundred cases.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses the fact that the derivative of profit is MR minus MC and sets it equal to zero
Solution with a calculator
Justification: $P'$ changes from positive to negative at this value, so the profit is greatest there

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the increase in total revenue when production is raised from $q=2$ to $q=6$ hundred cases. Show the setup for your calculation.
parts.model_answer: Increase in revenue $=R(6)-R(2)=\int_{2}^{6} MR(q)\,dq=59.349$ thousand dollars.

rubric_rows.criterion: Net change of the revenue as the definite integral of the marginal revenue over the given interval
Value with units

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The weekly fixed cost is $6$ thousand dollars, so $P(0)=-6$. Find the profit at the production level found in part (b). Does the workshop make a profit or a loss at that level?
parts.model_answer: $P(7.644)=P(0)+\int_0^{7.644}(MR(q)-MC(q))\,dq=-6+70.528=64.528$ thousand dollars, which is a profit.

rubric_rows.criterion: Profit as the initial value plus the integral of the marginal profit up to the production level of part (b)
Value of the profit and the conclusion

ap_calculus_ab-f04.title: Trench cross-section areas: trapezoid volume from a table, model volume, rate of change of area, average area and where it occurs

stimulus.description: Cross-sectional area of a trench, in square meters

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A drainage trench is dug along a straight line for $20$ meters. At the point $x$ meters from the start, the vertical cross section of the trench perpendicular to the line has area $A(x)$ square meters, where $A$ is a continuous function. Selected values of $A(x)$ are shown in the table. Use a trapezoidal sum with the five subintervals indicated by the table to approximate the volume of soil removed, $\int_0^{20} A(x)\,dx$. Using correct units, explain the meaning of this integral in the context of the problem.
parts.model_answer: Trapezoidal sum $=376.550$ cubic meters; $\int_0^{20} A(x)\,dx$ is the volume of the trench, i.e. of the soil removed, in cubic meters.

Approximation value

ap_calculus_ab-f05.title: Exponential decay differential equation: separation of variables, half-life, time to a given mass, average mass

stimulus.description: Radioactive tracer in a sealed capsule

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A sealed capsule holds $120$ grams of a radioactive tracer. Let $M(t)$ be the mass of the tracer, in grams, remaining $t$ years after the capsule is sealed. The rate at which the mass decreases is proportional to the mass present, so $\frac{dM}{dt}=-kM$ for a positive constant $k$. Use separation of variables to find an expression for $M(t)$ in terms of $k$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Separates the variables
Antiderivatives of both sides with a constant of integration
Solves for $M$ and uses the initial mass to find the constant

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The half-life of the tracer is $5$ years, that is, $M(5)=\frac12 M(0)$. Find $k$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of $k$ from the half-life condition

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: At what time $t$ will $12$ grams of the tracer remain? Express your answer in terms of natural logarithms.
parts.model_answer: $120e^{-kt}=12$ gives $e^{-kt}=\frac{1}{10}$, so $t=\frac{\ln 10}{k}=\frac{5\ln 10}{\ln 2}$ years.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets up and solves the exponential equation by taking logarithms
Value of $t$ with the value of $k$ substituted

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the average mass of the tracer in the capsule over the time interval $0\le t\le 10$ years. Give your answer in grams, in exact form.
parts.model_answer: $\frac{1}{10}\int_0^{10}120e^{-kt}\,dt=\frac{120}{10k}\left(1-e^{-10k}\right)=\frac{120}{10k}\left(1-\frac14\right)=\frac{45}{\log{\left(2 \right)}}$ grams.

rubric_rows.criterion: Integral setup for the average value, with division by the length of the interval
Antiderivative and evaluation using $e^{-10k}=\frac14$
Exact value of the average mass with units

blueprint.concept: Solve a proportional-decay differential equation by separation of variables, use the half-life to fix k, solve for the time at a given mass, and compute an exact average value

Use the half-life to get e^{-hk} = 1/2

key_conditions.condition: the mass after one half-life is half the initial mass

verification.independent_path: numerical quadrature for the average, Brent's root finder for the time, the half-life checked from the closed form with k = ln 2 / h, and the differential equation checked by central difference

ap_calculus_ab-f07.title: A function defined by its derivative: tangent approximation, concavity, substitution, absolute extrema

stimulus.description: A function given by its derivative and one value

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A function $f$ satisfies $f'(x)=-4xe^{-x^2}$ for all real $x$, and $f(1)=4$. Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve $y=f(x)$ at $x=1$, and use it to approximate $f\left(\frac32\right)$.
parts.model_answer: $f'(1)=- \frac{4}{e}$, so the tangent line is $y=4-\frac{4}{e}(x-1)$ and $f(3/2)\approx 4 - \frac{2}{e}$.

ap_calculus_ab-f08.title: Limits with L’Hospital’s Rule: a removable value, a repeated application, and a limit at infinity with a horizontal asymptote

stimulus.description: Three limit problems and a continuity condition

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find $\lim_{x\to 1}\frac{x^3-1}{\ln x}$. Show the work that leads to your answer, including why the method you use applies.
parts.model_answer: Substituting $x=1$ gives $\frac{0}{0}$, so L’Hospital’s Rule applies: $\lim_{x\to 1}\frac{3x^{2}}{1/x}=\lim_{x\to 1}3x^{3}=3$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the indeterminate form $\frac00$ (numerator and denominator both approach $0$)
Differentiates numerator and denominator
Value of the limit

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Let $g$ be the function defined by $g(x)=\frac{x^3-1}{\ln x}$ for $x>0$ with $x\ne 1$, and $g(1)=c$. For what value of $c$ is $g$ continuous at $x=1$? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $g$ is continuous at $x=1$ exactly when $\lim_{x\to 1}g(x)=g(1)$, so $c=3$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of $c$ with the condition that the limit equals the function value

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find $\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{e^x-1-x}{1x^2}$. Show the work that leads to your answer.
parts.model_answer: The form is $\frac{0}{0}$; L’Hospital’s Rule gives $\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{e^x-1}{2x}$, again $\frac{0}{0}$; applying it once more gives $\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{e^x}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the form $\frac00$ and applies L’Hospital’s Rule once
Recognizes that the new form is still $\frac00$ and applies the rule again
Value of the limit

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Let $h(x)=\frac{6x^2+5\ln x}{3x^2}$ for $x>0$. Find $\lim_{x\to\infty}h(x)$ and write an equation for the horizontal asymptote of the curve $y=h(x)$. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $h(x)=\frac{6}{3}+\frac{5}{3}\cdot\frac{\ln x}{x^2}$. The form $\frac{\ln x}{x^2}$ is $\frac{\infty}{\infty}$ and L’Hospital’s Rule gives $\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{1/x}{2x}=0$. So $\lim_{x\to\infty}h(x)=2$ and the horizontal asymptote is $y=2$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Shows $\frac{\ln x}{x^2}\to 0$ with a valid reason such as the $\frac{\infty}{\infty}$ form and the derivative ratio
Value of the limit and the equation of the asymptote

ap_calculus_ab-f09.title: Pen against a wall with different fence prices: cost function, critical value, second-derivative justification, minimum cost

stimulus.description: A pen built against a wall

data.costs: 6 dollars per meter perpendicular to the wall, 12 dollars per meter opposite the wall

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A farmer builds a rectangular pen against a long stone wall, so no fence is needed along the wall. The pen has area $150$ square meters and is divided into two stalls by one more fence perpendicular to the wall. Fence perpendicular to the wall costs $6$ dollars per meter, and the fence opposite the wall costs $12$ dollars per meter. Let $x$ meters be the length of each fence perpendicular to the wall. Write an expression for the total cost $C(x)$, in dollars, of the fence in terms of $x$ only.
parts.model_answer: The length opposite the wall is $\frac{150}{x}$ meters; three fences of length $x$ cost $18x$ and the fence opposite the wall costs $\frac{1800}{x}$, so $C(x)=18x+\frac{1800}{x}$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Length of the side opposite the wall from the area constraint
Total cost expression using three perpendicular fences and one fence opposite the wall

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the value of $x$ for which $C'(x)=0$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Derivative of the cost function
Solves for the positive critical value

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Use the second derivative to justify that the value of $x$ found in part (b) gives the absolute minimum cost over all possible values of $x$.
parts.model_answer: $C''(x)=\frac{3600}{x^{3}}$. For every $x>0$, $C''(x)>0$, so $C$ is concave up on its whole domain $x>0$. A concave-up function with $C'(10)=0$ has its absolute minimum at $x=10$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Second derivative of the cost function
Reason: $C''(x)>0$ for all $x>0$, the entire domain, so the function is concave up everywhere
Conclusion that the critical point is the absolute minimum

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the minimum total cost, in dollars, and the length, in meters, of the fence opposite the wall for that pen.
parts.model_answer: $C(10)=180+\frac{1800}{10}=360$ dollars; the fence opposite the wall has length $\frac{150}{10}=15$ meters.

rubric_rows.criterion: Minimum cost value
Length opposite the wall with units

ap_calculus_ab-f10.title: A rational function with unknown constants: critical-point conditions, limits at infinity, global extrema, number of solutions

stimulus.description: A rational function with unknown constants

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Let $f$ be the function given by $f(x)=\frac{Ax}{x^2+B}$, where $A$ and $B$ are positive constants. The function $f$ has a critical point at $x=3$, and $f(3)=3$. Find $A$ and $B$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Derivative of $f$ by the quotient rule
Uses $f'(p)=0$ to find $B$
Uses the value of $f$ to find $A$; both constants stated

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: For the values of $A$ and $B$ found in part (a), find $\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)$ and $\lim_{x\to-\infty}f(x)$, and give an equation for the horizontal asymptote of the curve $y=f(x)$.
parts.model_answer: Both limits equal $0$; the horizontal asymptote is $y=0$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Value of both limits and the equation of the horizontal asymptote

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Show that $f$ has an absolute maximum value of $3$ and an absolute minimum value of $-3$ on the interval $-\infty<x<\infty$. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: $f'(x)=\frac{18(9-x^2)}{(x^2+9)^2}$ is negative for $x<-3$, positive for $-3<x<3$, and negative for $x>3$. So $f$ has a relative minimum at $x=-3$ with $f(-3)=-3$ and a relative maximum at $x=3$ with $f(3)=3$. Since $f(x)\to 0$ as $x\to\pm\infty$ and $-3<0<3$, no value outside $[-3,3]$ occurs, so these are the absolute extreme values.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sign of $f'$ on the three intervals determined by the critical points
Classifies the critical points and gives the values of $f$ there
Reason that no other value is larger or smaller: the limits at infinity are $0$ and there are no other critical points

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: For which values of the constant $k$ does the equation $f(x)=k$ have exactly two solutions? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: On $(-\infty,-3]$, $f$ decreases from values near $0$ to $-3$; on $[-3,3]$, $f$ increases from $-3$ to $3$ and equals $0$ only at $x=0$; on $[3,\infty)$, $f$ decreases from $3$ toward $0$ without reaching it. By the Intermediate Value Theorem and monotonicity on each piece, each $k$ with $0<k<3$ is attained once on $(0,3)$ and once on $(3,\infty)$, and each $k$ with $-3<k<0$ is attained once on $(-\infty,-3)$ and once on $(-3,0)$. The values $k=0$ and $k=\pm 3$ give exactly one solution, and $|k|>3$ gives none. So the answer is $0<|k|<3$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes the behavior of $f$ on each of the intervals, including the values at the extremes
Conclusion with the Intermediate Value Theorem reason: exactly two solutions when $0<|k|<3$
